chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan from Ibn Muskan from Muhammad ibn Marwan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Jibraeel (peace be upon him) came to me and said: We, the group of angels, do not enter a house in which is a dog, nor a statue of a body, nor a vessel in which one urinates.'
ai.seo_question: What prevents angels from entering a house according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in al-Kafi, highlights the spiritual sensitivity of the angelic realm to physical impurities and idols, linking domestic cleanliness to divine presence. In Shia jurisprudence, this serves as a foundational proof for the rulings on *najāsah* (ritual impurity) and *tashabbuh* (resemblance to idols), emphasizing that the presence of angels is contingent upon the purity of the environment. It underscores the holistic nature of worship, where physical spaces are sanctified to facilitate spiritual connection.
